A pitch-level scouting model for this series: how each lineup handles the other staff's pitch mix, who wins each hitter vs starter matchup, how each manager runs his bullpen, and a plate-appearance-by-plate-appearance simulation of the full series. Every number on this page is rebuilt from raw Statcast data by the pipeline in this repository.

01 · Pitch mix

Run value against the pitches each staff actually throws

Each row is a pitch type. The grey bar is how often the opposing staff throws it. Next is the lineup's run value per 100 pitches against that pitch type, then the staff's run value with it, shown from the hitter's side so both bars read the same way. The edge column multiplies usage by the difference, so the total is an arsenal-weighted matchup score in runs per 100 pitches. These are raw season values, as Savant reports them.

Matchup score, runs per 100 pitches (hitter view)

■ red favors the hitter, ■ blue favors the pitcher. Staff = pitchers active in the last four weeks of the season.
02 · Player level

Hitter vs starter: expected wOBA from the outcome model

Each cell is the model's expected wOBA for that plate appearance: the hitter's outcome rates against the pitcher's hand and the pitcher's rates against the batter's side, combined with the odds-ratio method, then tilted by the pitch-mix edge if the backtest says the tilt helps. Click a cell for the outcome probabilities, the pitch-by-pitch breakdown and the zone overlay.

pitcher wins hitter wins (.255 · .315 · .375)
03 · Location

Where each lineup does damage vs where each staff throws

Statcast zones from the catcher's view: 1 to 9 is the strike zone, the four outer blocks are the chase areas. Left is the lineup's run value per 100 by zone, middle is where the opposing staff puts that pitch group, right is the staff's results by zone from the hitter's side.

05 · Starters

Projected starters and how long they last

Cards follow the rotation in the config. The simulator draws each starter's length from his own 2026 batters-faced distribution, capped for planned openers, and pulls him early if he gets hit hard.

06 · Bullpens

Bullpen tendencies, roles and situations

Roles come from how each reliever was actually used, not from saves. Leverage index (LI) measures how much a plate appearance could swing the win probability, so a 1.0 is average and 2.0 is twice as important. gmLI is a reliever's average leverage when he entered.

09 · Simulation

Plate-appearance-level series simulation

Every simulated game runs plate appearance by plate appearance: outcome probabilities from the model, league-average baserunning, starters pulled on their own usage patterns, relievers chosen by each manager's tendencies, and bullpen fatigue carried across the series calendar. Postseason rules apply, so there is no automatic runner in extra innings. The range comes from rerunning everything on bootstrap resamples of the season's games.

11 · Method

Method, definitions and caveats

Data. Every pitch of the season from Baseball Savant's Statcast search, plus Savant's Outs Above Average, sprint speed, catcher framing, baserunning and park factor leaderboards, and the MLB Stats API schedule (day/night, venue, temperature). The pipeline pulls, caches and refreshes them incrementally.

Run value. Change in run expectancy per pitch, summed per 100 pitches. Hitter view: positive means runs for the offense. Pitcher view: positive means runs saved. The model uses expected run value, which swaps each ball in play's actual result for its xwOBA, removing most defense and luck.

Shrinkage. Pitch-type values are regressed in two levels: pitch group toward league average, pitch type toward the player's own group value. Outcome rates use outcome-specific stabilization constants and a two-level platoon structure. Recent games count more (half-life set in the config).

Outcome model. Multinomial odds ratio over K, BB/HBP, 1B, 2B, 3B, HR and outs, with an optional pitch-mix tilt whose size is chosen on a validation window. Park factors apply by batter side, and home batters get a small tilt calibrated to an MLB-typical home win rate.

Caveats. Postseason managing is more aggressive than regular-season usage, which the leverage boost only approximates. Baserunning is league average. Lineups, rotations and bullpens come from the config file and should be updated when rosters are announced.

Sources: Baseball Savant Statcast Search, Savant Park Factors, Savant OAA, MLB Stats API.
